close_reason: Replaced .iter().map(|id| id.as_ref()).collect::<Vec<_>>() with direct result.created/updated/destroyed serialization at metadata.rs:160-162. Matches the canonical jmap-server::handlers::handle_changes shape exactly. Id is #[serde(transparent)] over String so wire format is byte-identical. cargo clippy --tests -- -D warnings clean; cargo test --all-features clean (44 + 3 + 24 + 1 tests pass).
description:
Scenario: metadata.rs:148-150 manually serializes the created/updated/destroyed arrays:

  "created":   result.created.iter().map(|id| id.as_ref()).collect::<Vec<_>>(),

The canonical jmap-server::handlers::handle_changes at handlers.rs:197-199 does the simpler:

  "created":   result.created,
  "updated":   result.updated,
  "destroyed": result.destroyed,

…because Id has #[serde(transparent)] (per the bd:JMAP-wlip.28 comment). The metadata handler's manual form works (Id and &str serialize to the same JSON string) but obscures the design choice and adds three lines of pointless adapter code.

Maintenance consequence:
(a) A future refactor that adds a property to Id (a tag, a hash, whatever) is masked by the &str collect. The direct Vec<Id> serialization would surface the JSON shape change immediately.
(b) The pattern teaches the wrong idiom to readers studying this crate as a reference for extension-server handler authoring.

Fix: replace metadata.rs:148-150 with the direct Vec<Id> form.
title: metadata-server's handle_metadata_changes manually serializes Id arrays via .iter().map(|id| id.as_ref()).collect::<Vec<_>>() rather than direct Vec<Id> serialization — extra code, hides the Id #[serde(transparent)] design
